channel.title: Frontier Wire
channel.description: AI news: frontier labs, research, policy and commentary.

item.title: AMD launches Zen 6 EPYC Venice processors with up to 256 cores
item.description: AMD has announced the availability of its EPYC 9006 \"Venice\" series processors featuring up to 256 Zen 6c cores per socket. The new enterprise processors utilize a 2nm manufacturing process and support up to 16 channels of DDR5-8000 or MRDIMM-12800 memory. The release of Zen 6 EPYC processors marks AMD's transition to a 2nm process node and introduces higher core counts for enterprise servers and HPC workloads.

item.title: OpenAI's adjusted operating margin improved to -109% in Q3
item.description: Leaked documents show OpenAI's adjusted operating margin improved from -150% in Q2 to -109% in Q3. During the same period, the company's revenue grew by roughly 50% to reach $10 billion. The leaked figures provide a rare look at OpenAI's financial performance, showing narrowing adjusted operating losses alongside rapid revenue growth driven by enterprise customers.

item.title: Amazon announces Ring AI security drone and roving business robot
item.description: Amazon's Ring launched a new robotics division debuting the Ring Drone Cam indoor flying camera for $249.99 and the Ring Rover Cam business robot for $999.99. Both autonomous devices use an AI Pilot system to map floor plans, navigate obstacles, and respond to security triggers. Amazon is expanding its consumer and enterprise security hardware ecosystem from stationary cameras into autonomous mobile robots.

item.title: CoreWeave reports Q3 revenue up 168% YoY to $3.66B and $132.5B backlog
item.description: CoreWeave reported third-quarter revenue of $3.66 billion, beating analyst estimates of $3.55 billion and marking a 168% year-over-year increase. The company also posted a net loss of $709 million and grew its revenue backlog to $132.5 billion. The financial results provide insight into neocloud infrastructure spending, debt financing, and customer demand amid questions about capital requirements for artificial intelligence buildouts.

item.title: OpenAI reports $10 billion in Q3 revenue as enterprise demand grows
item.description: OpenAI told investors its revenue jumped 50% to around $10 billion in the third quarter of 2026, up from 17% growth in the second quarter. More than half of the revenue came from enterprise clients, driven by demand for APIs and newer models like GPT-5.6 and Astra. The figures show rapid financial growth for leading AI labs, with enterprise clients and major partners like Microsoft capturing significant market activity.

item.title: Grok Build coding agent leaks confidential data from thousands of user apps
item.description: Security researchers found that thousands of apps created using SpaceXSI's Grok Build coding agent exposed confidential business, employee, and personal data because they could be accessed without sign-in. Out of 37,571 tested apps, 35,578 opened without authentication, including 24 internal apps belonging to SpaceXSI. The incident demonstrates how easy it is for AI coding tools to unintentionally publish sensitive corporate databases and internal documents to the public internet when proper access controls are missing by default.

item.title: Nvidia plans $10B investment in Anthropic alongside its IPO
item.description: Nvidia plans to invest $10 billion in Anthropic alongside its initial public offering. The commitment is part of a larger funding effort that includes public share sales and private deals with multiple technology giants. The investment highlights the deepening financial ties between major artificial intelligence labs and hardware providers as they secure massive capital deployments.

item.title: New York launches portal for AI safety law requiring developer registration
item.description: New York opened a registration portal for large frontier artificial intelligence developers as part of the RAISE Act. Companies with over $500 million in annual revenue must register by January 1, 2027, publish safety frameworks, and report critical safety incidents within 72 hours. The law establishes strict reporting and compliance requirements with penalties up to $3 million for large AI labs operating in New York.

item.title: Graphon Labs raises $35m Series A for AI agent memory infrastructure
item.description: Graphon Labs raised a $35 million Series A funding round led by RRE Ventures to scale persistent-memory infrastructure for AI agents. The round brings the 20-person startup's total funding to $43.3 million. The funding highlights growing investor and enterprise focus on solving AI agent memory and context limitations beyond standard context windows.

item.title: Anthropic brings Claude assistant to Google Meet for live workplace tasks
item.description: Anthropic launched Claude Meetings in beta on Google Meet, allowing its AI assistant to join video calls as a visible participant to draft plans and answer questions in real time. The company also announced Claude Whiteboards and Claude Sheets alongside a roadshow for its US initial public offering. The release marks an expansion of AI tools designed to shift workplace assistance from post-meeting summaries to real-time task execution during video calls, as companies compete to offer comprehensive office suites.

item.title: Anthropic sets IPO price range aiming for up to $1.4 trillion valuation
item.description: Anthropic submitted an updated S-1 filing for an IPO and concurrent private placement aiming to raise up to $88.5 billion. The offering sets a share price range of $70 to $78, implying a fully diluted valuation of up to $1.4 trillion. This public market debut represents one of the largest capital raises in history and signals major financial scaling for a leading AI developer amid shifting market conditions.

item.title: Anthropic launches Claude Whiteboards, Sheets, and Data
item.description: Anthropic is rolling out Claude Whiteboards and Claude Sheets in beta, alongside Claude Data, to let paid users collaborate with the assistant on shared planning, spreadsheets, and data. The tools operate on web, desktop, and mobile, allowing teams to keep documents within Claude before exporting to partner platforms. This release integrates planning, spreadsheets, and data analysis directly into Claude workspaces, reducing the need to move project outputs to separate external applications.

item.title: Anthropic co-founders to sell $1.75 billion in shares ahead of $1.4 trillion IPO
item.description: Anthropic's seven co-founders will each sell about $250 million worth of stock, totaling $1.75 billion, as the company files an IPO offering 825 million Class A shares at $70‑$78 each. The offering could value the company at up to $1.404 trillion. The sale provides a major liquidity event and underscores the scale of capital flowing into AI firms.

item.title: Mercor raises $750 million Series D, valuation jumps to $20 billion
item.description: AI training startup Mercor announced a $750 million Series D funding round that values the company at $20 billion, double its October 2025 valuation. Investors include Benchmark, General Catalyst, Nvidia and others. The capital boost expands Mercor’s ability to connect firms with experts for training AI models, a growing need as more companies develop specialized AI agents.

item.title: Google rolls out Gemini 4 Carbon to the public with agent swarm feature
item.description: Google is rolling out Gemini 4 Carbon to the general public via the Gemini API, the Gemini app and Antigravity, after a two-week limited release to cybersecurity defenders. The model is priced at $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens during an introductory period, and Google is previewing a "swarm" feature that turns a single prompt into a coordinated team of agents. Google's public release of Carbon, priced well below rival frontier models, intensifies competition among the top AI labs and brings long-horizon agentic capabilities to a wider developer base.

item.title: Google unveils TPU 8tx and TPU 8i Max for confidential and large-scale AI workloads
item.description: Google on Monday unveiled two new variants of its eighth-generation tensor processing units, TPU 8tx and TPU 8i Max, targeting confidential inference and larger memory capacity for AI workloads. The 8tx, designed with AMD, is built for secure workloads, while the 8i Max combines two TPU 8i chips to double memory, processing power and bandwidth. Google's expanded TPU lineup gives enterprises and governments an in-house alternative to Nvidia for running AI on sensitive data and large workloads, adding to the push by hyperscalers to reduce reliance on external chipmakers.

item.title: TSMC to invest up to $1B in Anthropic and OpenAI at IPO price
item.description: TSMC has approved up to $500 million to buy shares in Anthropic at its IPO price and up to $500 million for preferred stock in OpenAI. The move follows Anthropic's IPO pricing of $70 to $78 per share and reflects TSMC's confidence in AI demand. It shows a major chipmaker backing key AI developers, potentially influencing AI supply chains and investment flows.

item.title: Fable 5.2 tops Remote Labor Index at 41.3% of freelance jobs
item.description: On the Remote Labor Index from Scale Labs and the Center for AI Safety, Anthropic's Fable 5.2 completes 41.3% of real freelance projects at professional quality, ahead of Opus 5.5 (21.25%) and GPT 6 Astra (20.83%). The score is up from 2.5% for the top system a year ago. The RLI measures how often AI output is acceptable to paying clients, making it a direct gauge of how close AI agents are to doing real freelance work.

item.title: Anthropic sets IPO price at $70–$78 per share, targeting $1.4 trillion valuation
item.description: Anthropic filed an updated IPO prospectus on November 10, 2026, offering 825 million Class A shares at $70–$78 per share, implying a valuation of up to $1.404 trillion. The company expects to raise $57.75–$64.35 billion from the public offering, with total net proceeds of $84.6–$93.7 billion including a $26 billion private sale to AMD, Broadcom, Google, Micron, Microsoft, Nvidia and TSMC. Anthropic's IPO at a valuation below its earlier $2 trillion target reflects a broader pullback in AI investing and sets a new benchmark for how public markets value frontier AI companies.

item.title: IBM and Microsoft announce Imagine Enterprise AI agent platform
item.description: IBM and Microsoft announced Imagine Enterprise, an agentic platform designed to help enterprises build, run, and govern AI agents for industry-specific processes. The platform combines Microsoft's cloud and security technologies with over 6,000 prebuilt AI agents and assets from IBM Consulting. The partnership brings together Microsoft's technology stack with IBM Consulting's industry expertise and prebuilt agents to help regulated enterprises deploy AI into production.

item.title: Google Cloud launches Gemini for healthcare
item.description: Google Cloud has launched Gemini for healthcare, an AI solution designed to unify clinical, operational, and administrative systems. The platform is initially available in preview with launch partners including HCA Healthcare, Highmark Health, and Northwell Health. The platform addresses administrative burdens in healthcare by synthesizing records and orchestrating workflows within defined guardrails.

item.title: Cyberattacks threaten to make open-source AI less open, Hugging Face warns
item.description: Hugging Face executive Irene Solaiman warned that a string of cyberattacks and security breaches targeting open AI platforms risks forcing open-source AI to become less open. Recent incidents include an October attack on OpenCode that compromised third-party API keys and a summer breach where an OpenAI agent swarm accessed Hugging Face infrastructure. Security incidents and breaches at open-source AI platforms create tension between maintaining an open, permissive community for independent researchers and implementing strict access controls to prevent cyberattacks.

item.title: Alibaba chip unit T-Head files confidential Hong Kong IPO application
item.description: Alibaba Group's chip unit, T-Head, submitted a confidential listing application for a Hong Kong initial public offering after receiving approval to proceed with a spin-off. The proposed offering includes a Hong Kong public share sale and an institutional placement, though the deal size and structure have not yet been determined. This spin-off allows investors to separately value Alibaba's core businesses and T-Head while enabling the semiconductor unit to raise capital independently.

item.title: Cognizant forms Claude Frontier Capability Group with 25,000 staff
item.description: Cognizant formed the Claude Frontier Capability Group, committing over 25,000 professionals to deliver Anthropic's AI assistant for clients. The IT company has also trained or certified more than 44,000 associates on Claude and introduced a managed services model for production operations. This move highlights how major IT services providers are dedicating tens of thousands of certified personnel to deploy and manage frontier AI models for corporate clients.

item.title: Froncort.AI raises $2.3M from Google.org to expand AI disease surveillance
item.description: Pune-based healthcare AI startup Froncort.AI has raised $2.3 million from Google.org, plus $200K in Google Cloud credits and pro bono technical expertise, to develop mAI-NETRA, a mobile version of its AI disease surveillance platform. The funding will extend the platform to six infectious diseases across up to eight high-burden districts in three Indian states, covering two to three million people. The funding shows AI being applied to a practical public-health problem—directing limited screening resources to high-risk areas—rather than to consumer products.

item.title: DeepMind unveils AlphaProof Code for deep software verification
item.description: DeepMind announced AlphaProof Code, an AI system designed to verify complex software at depth. The tool aims to improve code security and correctness. It provides a more thorough automated way to check software, reducing bugs and vulnerabilities for developers and users.

item.title: TSMC October revenue hits record $17.81bn on AI chip demand
item.description: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC) reported its highest-ever monthly revenue in October at NT$586.89 billion ($17.81 billion), a 59.7% increase year-on-year. The growth was driven by continued demand for advanced semiconductors used in artificial intelligence applications. As the world's largest contract chipmaker, TSMC's record financial results provide a direct indicator of the scale of hardware investment across the artificial intelligence industry.

item.title: Anthropic releases Claude Fable and Mythos 5.2 models
item.description: Anthropic released Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2, upgrading models designed for complex technical challenges with improvements in coding, reasoning, and vision. Fable 5.2 is available immediately to all users, while Mythos 5.2 is restricted to vetted organizations. The release demonstrates the expanding capabilities of AI models on complex technical and scientific tasks, alongside ongoing efforts to balance public availability with cybersecurity and biology safeguards.

item.title: OpenAI launches Business Hub and verified Business Agents in ChatGPT beta
item.description: OpenAI announced a beta Business Hub that lets companies create verified business profiles and launch custom Business Agents in ChatGPT. The features provide limited insights such as profile views and allow users to ask product questions. It expands ChatGPT’s role as a consumer discovery platform, giving businesses a new AI‑driven channel to reach users.

item.title: Meituan releases weights for LongCat-2.5 under MIT license
item.description: Meituan released the open weights for LongCat-2.5, a 1.6T-parameter MoE model for long-horizon agentic tasks with vision, under the MIT license on November 9. The release comes one week after the model was introduced on November 1. The release makes a 1.6T-parameter MoE model available under a permissive open license for developers and researchers.
